title: The Man Who Doubted the Machine
claim: In 1983 a Soviet duty officer judged a satellite launch warning to be false, and he was right.

sources.title: September 1983: Soviet officer defies military protocol, averting potential nuclear war

beats.text: The computer said America had just launched a nuclear missile.
beats.note: One ICBM reported heading toward the Soviet Union from the United States.

beats.text: It's just after midnight, September 26th, 1983. Stanislav Petrov is on duty in a bunker outside Moscow.
beats.note: Wikipedia: 'Shortly after midnight, the bunker's computers reported that one intercontinental ballistic missile was heading toward the Soviet Union from the United States.' Petrov, a lieutenant colonel, was the officer on duty at Serpukhov-15 near Moscow.

beats.text: Weeks earlier, Soviet forces shot down a Korean airliner.
beats.note: KAL 007 was shot down on 1 September 1983.

beats.text: Then the screen lights up. One missile. Then four more.
beats.note: One ICBM reported first; later four more.

beats.text: His job: watch the satellites and warn his superiors.
beats.note: He monitored the Oko satellite early-warning network; his responsibilities included notifying superiors of any impending nuclear missile attack.

beats.text: But Petrov reasons that a real first strike would be massive. Five makes no sense.
beats.note: He cited his belief and training that any U.S. first strike would be massive, so five missiles seemed an illogical start.

beats.text: So he waits for proof. None arrives.
beats.note: He decided to wait for corroborating evidence, of which none arrived.

beats.text: The cause? Sunlight glinting off high clouds, lined up with the satellites' orbits.
beats.note: A rare alignment of sunlight on high-altitude clouds and the satellites' Molniya orbits.

beats.text: The world learned of it fifteen years later.
beats.note: General Yuri Votintsev first revealed it to the public in 1998.

beats.text: One man trusted his doubt over a machine.
beats.note: Ends on the opening composition so the video loops into the hook.
